**Why:** The sidebar should reflect exactly what's visible on the map so users can navigate to filtered results. Showing 26 items when only 7 are visible on the map is misleading.

**Acceptance criteria:**

title: This Day in History: highlight apparitions by feast day
description:
Add a 'This Day in History' indicator that highlights apparitions whose feast day (or anniversary date) matches today's date. Today is 2026-06-06.

**Why:** Creates a daily discovery hook — users visiting on a feast day see immediate relevance. Adds a spiritual dimension beyond just browsing.

**Implementation plan:**
1. Add feastDay (MM-DD) field to apparitions data — either the canonical feast day or the anniversary of the first apparition
2. On app load, check today's month/day against each apparition's feastDay
3. If match(es) found: show a subtle 'Today's Feast' banner/badge, highlight the matching pin(s) with a special glow, auto-open the sidebar entry or show a toast notification
4. If no match: feature is silent (no UI change)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Matching apparitions get a visual indicator (highlighted pin + sidebar badge)
- A dismissable banner shows 'Today is the feast day of [name]'
- Works correctly across all months/days
- Graceful when no feast day matches today
design: Feast day data can be sourced from Catholic calendar / shrine records. Each apparition has a known feast or anniversary. Add as a feastDay: 'MM-DD' field in apparitions.ts.
close_reason: feastDay field added to all 26 apparitions. TodayFeastBanner component created with dismissable UI. Feast Day badge shown in sidebar list items on matching days.

title: Medjugorje Messages page: analytics + geopolitical timeline
description:
Add a new /medjugorje route reachable via a button on the main map page. This page displays Our Lady of Medjugorje messages (sourced from medjugorje.ws/en/messages) alongside Claude-powered NLP analytics and a curated geopolitical events timeline.

**Why this exists:** Medjugorje is the most prolific ongoing private revelation (1981–present), generating hundreds of messages. Visualizing these messages against world history gives a data science lens on the apparition — letting users see correlations between the messages' themes (prayer, urgency, peace) and geopolitical events of the time.

**Core components:**
1. Nav button on main map page that routes to /medjugorje
2. Message data — pre-scraped from medjugorje.ws and bundled as a TS data file (avoids CORS); include a 'Refresh from source' flow via Vite proxy for latest messages
3. Claude-powered NLP pipeline — sentiment analysis over time, keyword/theme clustering, topic shifts; Claude makes recommendations and explains patterns
4. Curated geopolitical events dataset (1981–present): major wars, collapses, disasters, papal events; bundled as a TS data file
5. Claude enrichment — for a selected message or time window, Claude explains how the message's themes relate to concurrent world events
6. Visual analytics — timeline of messages with sentiment overlay, keyword frequency heatmap, theme clustering chart, event correlation markers on the timeline

**Design language:** Match the celestial dark theme of the main app. Timeline as the primary axis. Analytics panels slide in like the detail panel on the map.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Button on main page navigates to /medjugorje without breaking map state
- Messages display with date, full text, and source attribution
- At least 3 analytics visualizations (sentiment trend, keyword heatmap, theme clusters)
- Geopolitical events appear on the same timeline axis as messages
- Claude enrichment runs on demand (button) for any selected time window
- No new backend process — all powered by Vite + React + Anthropic SDK
design: Routing: React Router (add if not present) or hash-based routing. Data: messages and events as bundled TS files with a refresh mechanism. Analytics: Claude API with structured output for NLP results, charted with a lightweight viz lib (recharts or d3). User has ML/DS background — Claude sets up the pipeline architecture, user may tune models/prompts.
